angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 163,490 km at 48.46 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 20.6355 +/- 0.0190 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 48.46 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.235 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Pozuelos et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2096 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...672A..70P/abstract): 163,490 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.231 +/- 0.012 solar masses from Pozuelos et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2096 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...672A..70P/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3300 +/- 50 K from Pozuelos et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2096 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...672A..70P/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Pozuelos et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2096 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...672A..70P/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2096.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.060, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
